**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

Section 20 sits at the **preferred** position on every element:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Express duty to defend Customer + affiliates | § 20.1 "defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents" |
| Third-party claim indemnity | § 20.1 / § 20.2 |
| Services/Deliverables IP infringement | § 20.1 |
| Vendor's breach of applicable law | § 20.2 |
| Data breach caused by Vendor | § 20.2 "unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor" |
| Gross negligence / wilful misconduct | § 20.2 (plus fraud) |
| Notice / control / cooperation | § 20.4 |
| Narrow Customer indemnity | § 20.3 — unmodified Customer-supplied material and Customer's violation of Applicable Law only |

Additional points in our favour, noted rather than flagged:

- **No IP-indemnity exclusions.** § 20.1 carries none of the usual Customer modification/combination/specification carve-outs, so it is stronger than the fallback.
- **Uncapped.** § 21.3 makes indemnification obligations an Excluded Claim, so Vendor's indemnity escapes the § 21.1 cap. The fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap would be a downgrade, so I did not propose it.
- **Remedy ladder present anyway.** § 20.5 requires procure / modify / replace and, failing that, termination with a refund of prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services.
- **Procedure protections run our way**: cooperation is at the indemnifying party's expense, delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice, and Vendor cannot settle by admitting our fault or without fully releasing us.

The only sub-preferred detail worth a mention in negotiation rather than a redline is the refund basis in § 20.5 (straight-line three-year amortisation of prepaid and implementation Fees), which is a commercial calibration, not a fallback failure.
